nations.name: Paiwan
nations.lands: Southern Central Mountain Range across Pingtung and Taitung counties, Taiwan

facts.text: About 102,730 Paiwan people were counted in January 2020, living in the southern mountains of Pingtung and Taitung.
The Ravar branch of the Paiwan is known for outstanding carving and pottery.

nations.name: Wanniyala-Aetto
nations.lands: Eastern Sri Lanka, including the Maduru Oya area

facts.text: In 1983, 51,468 hectares of Wanniyala-Aetto customary land were declared the Maduru Oya National Park.
Their own name, Wanniyala-Aetto, means forest dwellers, and their ancestors lived on the island long before the Sinhalese and the Tamils arrived.

nations.name: Tsou
nations.lands: Alishan Township in Chiayi County, plus Nantou and Kaohsiung, Taiwan

facts.text: The Tsou homeland centres on Alishan Township in Chiayi County, southwest of Yushan in central Taiwan.
The Tsou population was 6,702 in January 2020.

nations.name: Mentawai
nations.lands: The Mentawai Islands, including Siberut, off West Sumatra, Indonesia

facts.text: On Siberut, a UNESCO biosphere reserve since 1981, Mentawai communities use the forest with care, guided by traditional knowledge.

source.title: Siberut Biosphere Reserve, Indonesia
source.publisher: UNESCO Man and the Biosphere Programme

facts.text: Siberut, home to many Mentawai communities, is the largest of the four Mentawai Islands west of Sumatra.

source.title: Siberut Biosphere Reserve, Indonesia
source.publisher: UNESCO Man and the Biosphere Programme

nations.name: Lumad
nations.lands: Mindanao, Philippines

facts.text: Lumad is a shared name for many Indigenous peoples of Mindanao, among them the Manobo, Subanon, Mandaya, Talandig and Teduray.
Lumad advocacy, with allies, helped write two important provisions into the 1987 Philippine Constitution.

nations.name: Khasi
nations.lands: Khasi Hills of Meghalaya, India, and nearby Bangladesh

facts.text: The Khasi Hills Autonomous District Council has a wing that oversees the Elakas, the traditional Khasi states.

source.title: General Administration Department and Elaka Administration

facts.text: Apart from Shillong's municipality and cantonment, all of Meghalaya is governed under the Sixth Schedule, the only northeast state where this is so.

nations.name: Bunun
nations.lands: Both sides of the Central Mountain Range in Nantou, Hualien, Taitung and Kaohsiung, Taiwan

facts.text: The Bunun live higher in the mountains than any other Indigenous people in Taiwan, mostly between 500 and 1,500 metres.
About 59,536 Bunun people were counted in January 2020, with homes in Nantou, Hualien, Taitung and Kaohsiung.

nations.name: Tamang
nations.lands: Hills around the Kathmandu Valley and central Nepal

facts.text: The Tamang are on the Nepal government's official list of Adivasi Janajati, or Indigenous nationalities.

source.title: Adivasi Janajati list
source.publisher: National Foundation for Development of Indigenous Nationalities, Nepal

facts.text: Tamang is the mother tongue of about 4.88 percent of Nepal's population, according to the 2021 census.

nations.name: Akha
nations.lands: Northern Thailand, eastern Myanmar and northern Laos

facts.text: The Akha are one of more than 20 highland Indigenous peoples of northern Thailand.

nations.name: Saisiyat
nations.lands: Hsinchu and Miaoli counties in northwestern Taiwan

facts.text: The Saisiyat live in northwestern Taiwan, in Hsinchu County and Miaoli County on either side of Ngangihaw mountain.
The Saisiyat population was 6,730 in January 2020.

nations.name: Truku
nations.lands: Xiulin, Wanrong and Zhuoxi townships in Hualien County, Taiwan

facts.text: The Truku were officially recognized as one of Taiwan's Indigenous peoples in 2004.
About 32,333 Truku people were counted in January 2020, mostly in Hualien County.

nations.name: Sediq
nations.lands: Mountain areas of Nantou and Hualien in central Taiwan

facts.text: Three subgroups make up the Sediq, each with its own group identity: Seediq Tgdaya, Sediq Toda and Sejiq Truku.
About 10,452 Sediq people were counted in January 2020, mostly in the mountains of Nantou and Hualien.

nations.name: Bhil
nations.lands: Madhya Pradesh, Gujarat, Rajasthan and Maharashtra, India

facts.text: India's government names the Bhil among the tribal peoples whose movements strengthened the country's freedom struggle.

source.title: Cabinet approves declaration of 15th November as Janjatiya Gaurav Divas
source.publisher: Prime Minister's Office, Government of India

nations.name: Marma
nations.lands: Chittagong Hill Tracts of Bangladesh

facts.text: Together, the Chakma, Marma and Tripura make up about 90 percent of the Indigenous peoples of the Chittagong Hill Tracts.

nations.name: Yakthung
nations.lands: Limbuwan in the eastern hills of Nepal, including Taplejung, Panchthar, Terhathum and Ilam, plus Jhapa, Morang and Sunsari, with communities in Sikkim and Darjeeling, India

facts.text: In Nepal's 2021 census, 84.5 percent of Yakthung people reported Limbu as their mother tongue, a language with its own script, Sirijanga.

source.title: लिम्बु (Limbu)
source.publisher: National Foundation for Development of Indigenous Nationalities, Nepal

facts.text: In 2021 Nepal's Language Commission recommended Limbu, alongside Maithili, as an official language of Province 1 in eastern Nepal.

source.title: Language Commission recommends province-wise official languages before government

nations.name: Tharu
nations.lands: The Terai plains of southern Nepal, and neighbouring India

facts.text: The Tharu are on the Nepal government's official list of Adivasi Janajati, or Indigenous nationalities.

source.title: Adivasi Janajati list
source.publisher: National Foundation for Development of Indigenous Nationalities, Nepal

facts.text: Tharu is the mother tongue of about 5.88 percent of Nepal's population, according to the 2021 census.

nations.name: Kurukh
nations.lands: Jharkhand, Odisha, Chhattisgarh and West Bengal in India, with communities in Assam, Bangladesh and Nepal

facts.text: Odisha counted 358,112 Kurukh (Oraon) people in 2011; many farm and practice crafts such as carpentry, rope making and weaving date palm leaf mats.

source.title: Odisha State Tribal Museum: Oraon
source.publisher: Odisha State Tribal Museum (SCSTRTI, Government of Odisha)

facts.text: Twelve to thirty Kurukh villages join in a Parha council, where members of each village council meet under a Parha chief.

source.title: Oraon
source.publisher: Dr. Ramdayal Munda Tribal Welfare Research Institute, Jharkhand

nations.name: Thao
nations.lands: Ita Thao Village by Sun Moon Lake and Dapinglin, Nantou County, Taiwan

facts.text: Thao people live mainly in Ita Thao Village in Yuchi Township and in Dapinglin, Shuili Township, both in Nantou County. They numbered about 817 in January 2020.
Thao oral history tells of ancestors who followed a white deer to Sun Moon Lake and found a fertile place full of fish.

nations.name: Pinuyumayan
nations.lands: Taitung City and Beinan Township on the Taitung Plain, Taiwan

facts.text: Taitung City and Beinan Township on the Taitung Plain are the heart of Pinuyumayan life today.
About 14,517 Pinuyumayan people were counted in January 2020, and many have moved from eastern Taiwan to cities, where they are active in many fields.

nations.name: Santal
nations.lands: Jharkhand, West Bengal, Odisha and nearby states of India, northwest Bangladesh, and Nepal

facts.text: On 25 December 2025, India's Constitution was released in the Santali language, written in the Ol Chiki script.

source.title: President of India releases the Constitution of India in the Santhali language

facts.text: Santali, the Santal language, is one of the 22 languages listed in the Eighth Schedule of India's Constitution.

source.title: Languages Included in the Eighth Schedule of the Indian Constitution
source.publisher: Department of Official Language, Ministry of Home Affairs, India

nations.name: Munda
nations.lands: Jharkhand, Odisha, West Bengal, Chhattisgarh and Bihar in India, with communities in Bangladesh

facts.text: Mundari has its own script, known in the community as Mundari Bani; a version reformed in 2008 by Munda community bodies is in the Unicode Standard.

source.title: Chapter 13, South and Central Asia-II (The Unicode Standard, Version 18.0)

facts.text: Munda call their dance durang and their song susun, and both women and men dance at social events and seasonal festivals.

source.title: Munda
source.publisher: Dr. Ramdayal Munda Tribal Welfare Research Institute, Jharkhand

nations.name: Ho
nations.lands: Kolhan region of Jharkhand and northern Odisha, with communities in West Bengal and Bihar, India

facts.text: In Odisha, Ho farmers grow paddy, maize and ragi, tend kitchen gardens, and gather mushrooms, mahua and greens from the forest.

source.title: Odisha State Tribal Museum: Ho
source.publisher: Odisha State Tribal Museum (SCSTRTI, Government of Odisha)

facts.text: The Ho language has its own recently devised alphabet, Warang Citi, which is encoded in the Unicode Standard and used by a yearly and a biweekly publication.

source.title: Chapter 13, South and Central Asia-II (The Unicode Standard, Version 18.0)

nations.name: Kanakanavu
nations.lands: Namaxia District, Kaohsiung City, Taiwan

facts.text: On June 26, 2014, Taiwan's government recognized the Kanakanavu as an independent people, the 16th on the official list.
Some Kanakanavu people understand their name as people living in a forest of Taiwan giant bamboo.

nations.name: Rai
nations.lands: Majh Kirat, also called Khambuwan, in the middle hills of eastern Nepal between the Dudh Koshi and Arun rivers, plus Jhapa, Morang, Sunsari and the Kathmandu Valley

facts.text: The Kirat Rai Yayokkha, founded in 1990, works to unite Nepal's diverse Rai communities and to promote Rai languages, arts and literature.
The Rai are a multilingual people: the Kirat Rai Yayokkha has registered 26 Rai language groups, among them Bantawa, Chamling and Kulung.

source.title: राई (Rai)
source.publisher: National Foundation for Development of Indigenous Nationalities, Nepal

nations.name: Rukai
nations.lands: Southern Central Mountain Range in Kaohsiung, Pingtung and Taitung, Taiwan

facts.text: About 13,465 Rukai people were counted in January 2020, living in Kaohsiung, Pingtung and Taitung.
For the Rukai, the lily stands for purity and courage, and the right to wear lily ornaments sits at the heart of their culture.

nations.name: Gond
nations.lands: Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Maharashtra, Telangana, Odisha and neighboring states of central India

facts.text: Masaram Gondi, a script created in 1918 by Munshi Mangal Singh Masaram of Madhya Pradesh to write the Gondi language, is still used today in handwritten and printed materials.

source.title: Chapter 13, South and Central Asia-II (The Unicode Standard, Version 18.0)

facts.text: Gond painting, mostly made in Patangarh village in Dindori district, gained worldwide recognition after shows in Tokyo and Paris and became a livelihood for many tribal families.

source.title: Gond Art: Details about Gond Tribal Art and Painting of India

nations.name: Dayak
nations.lands: Borneo: Kalimantan (Indonesia), Sabah and Sarawak (Malaysia) and Brunei

facts.text: Dayak is a shared name for many Indigenous peoples of Borneo, by some estimates about 450 ethnolinguistic groups.
Dayak peoples share traditions of longhouse living and customary law known as adat.

nations.name: Wurundjeri Woi Wurrung
nations.lands: Melbourne and surrounding lands, including the Birrarung (Yarra River), Victoria, Australia

facts.text: The Wurundjeri council was set up in 1985 by Wurundjeri descendants and gained Registered Aboriginal Party status for cultural heritage in 2008.

source.title: Recent Past & Present
source.publisher: Wurundjeri Woi Wurrung Cultural Heritage Aboriginal Corporation

facts.text: In 2017 a Yarra River protection bill was the first legislation put before Victoria's parliament with a dual Aboriginal language title: Wilip-gin Birrarung murron, keep the Birrarung alive.

source.title: Recent Past & Present
source.publisher: Wurundjeri Woi Wurrung Cultural Heritage Aboriginal Corporation

nations.name: iTaukei
nations.lands: Fiji

facts.text: The iTaukei Land Trust Board, set up in 1940, manages iTaukei land for its owners, whether a yavusa, mataqali or tokatoka.
The iTaukei Affairs Board, set up in 1944 as the Fijian Affairs Board, is the main advisory and coordinating body for iTaukei affairs, supporting village, tikina and provincial leaders.

nations.name: Kosraeans
nations.lands: Kosrae, an island state in the east of the Federated States of Micronesia, with the municipalities of Lelu, Malem, Tafunsak and Utwe

facts.text: Kosrae State has its own constitutional government, with a legislature elected by voters in the districts of Lelu, Malem, Tafunsak and Utwe.

source.title: Kosrae
source.publisher: Legal Information System of the Federated States of Micronesia

facts.text: In 2017 Kosraean elders proposed protecting Kosrae's mountain range, seen as the figure Mahkontowe, now the Mahkontowe Conservation Area under Kosrae State law.

nations.name: Moriori
nations.lands: Rēkohu and Rangihaute (the Chatham and Pitt Islands), Aotearoa New Zealand

facts.text: Moriori are the Indigenous people of Rēkohu and Rangihaute, the Chatham Islands, and are represented by the Hokotehi Moriori Trust.
The Hokotehi Moriori Trust takes part in key parts of the Rēkohu economy, such as fishing, farming and tourism.

nations.name: Gadigal
nations.lands: The southern side of Sydney Harbour (Port Jackson), from South Head to around Petersham, in Sydney, New South Wales, Australia

facts.text: Descendants of the Eora still live in Sydney today and proudly use the name Eora.
The City of Sydney formally acknowledges the Gadigal of the Eora Nation as the traditional custodians of the place now called Sydney.

nations.name: Larrakia
nations.lands: The Darwin region, from Cox Peninsula in the west to Gunn Point in the north, Northern Territory, Australia

facts.text: Larrakia Nation Aboriginal Corporation, set up in 1997, runs about 40 programs in Darwin, including the Larrakia Land and Sea Rangers.
Larrakia are the traditional owners of the Darwin region, with country reaching from Cox Peninsula in the west up to Gunn Point in the north.

nations.name: Marshallese
nations.lands: the atolls and islands of the Republic of the Marshall Islands, including Majuro

facts.text: Waan Aelõñ in Majel, Canoes of the Marshall Islands, is a Majuro program that trains young Marshallese women and men in skills for a sustainable future.

source.title: Canoes of the Marshall Islands, Waan Aelõñ in Majel

facts.text: A Marshallese stick chart maps how ocean swells bend around islands, with cowrie shells for the islands, and is studied before a voyage rather than used at sea.

source.title: Stick Navigation Chart
source.publisher: Smithsonian National Museum of Natural History

nations.name: Kaurna
nations.lands: The Adelaide Plains of South Australia, from around Crystal Brook in the north, bounded by the Mount Lofty Ranges to the east, Australia

facts.text: In March 2018 Kaurna people were recognised as native title holders around Adelaide, the first positive native title determination over a capital city area.

source.title: Native Title Recognition For Kaurna People Over Adelaide Area

facts.text: Requests for Kaurna names and translations all go through Kaurna Warra Karrpanthi, an Aboriginal corporation.

source.title: Aboriginal people of South Australia: Kaurna

nations.name: Torres Strait Islanders
nations.lands: the islands of the Torres Strait between Cape York and Papua New Guinea, in Queensland, Australia, and the Northern Peninsula Area

facts.text: The Torres Strait Regional Authority, an Australian Government body set up on 1 July 1994, counts recognising and maintaining Torres Strait Islander Ailan Kastom among its functions.
Kala Lagaw Ya is the traditional language of the western and central Torres Strait islands, and Meriam Mir is the language of the eastern islands.

nations.name: Noongar
nations.lands: The south-west of Western Australia, including the Perth region, Australia

facts.text: Western Australia's settlement recognises the Noongar people as the traditional owners of the South-West, with about A$1.3 billion in land and other benefits.

source.title: All six South West Native Title Settlement Agreements registered

facts.text: The South West Native Title Settlement covers about 200,000 square kilometres and affects an estimated 40,000 Noongar people.

source.title: South West Aboriginal Land and Sea Council
source.publisher: South West Aboriginal Land and Sea Council

nations.name: Yolŋu
nations.lands: North-east Arnhem Land, including the Gove Peninsula, Northern Territory, Australia

facts.text: Yolŋu elders founded Dhimurru Aboriginal Corporation to manage their land on the Gove Peninsula and the visitors who come to it.

source.title: Only Yolŋu make decisions for this land
source.publisher: Office of the Registrar of Indigenous Corporations (Australian Government)

facts.text: The name Dhimurru means east wind, the wind that carries the monsoon rains and brings new life to the land.

source.title: Only Yolŋu make decisions for this land
source.publisher: Office of the Registrar of Indigenous Corporations (Australian Government)

nations.name: Waikato-Tainui
nations.lands: The Waikato region of the North Island, Aotearoa New Zealand

facts.text: Waikato-Tainui describes itself as a growing tribe of over 90,000 people, voyagers and pioneers like their ancestors.

source.title: Ko Waikato te iwi, ko Tainui te waka

facts.text: Waikato-Tainui celebrate their identity as people of the Tainui waka and as protectors of the Kiingitanga movement.

source.title: Ko Waikato te iwi, ko Tainui te waka

nations.name: Niueans
nations.lands: the island of Niue in the South Pacific, with villages such as Alofi, Mutalau and Toi

facts.text: Fale Tāoga Niue, home of the Niue National Museum, opened on 19 October 2018, the anniversary of the Niue Constitution Celebrations.
Niue's Vagahau Niue Act 2012 recognises Vagahau Niue as the official language of Niue and created the Niue Language Commission to protect it.

source.title: Vagahau Niue Act 2012
source.publisher: Université Laval, CEFAN: L'aménagement linguistique dans le monde

nations.name: Samoans
nations.lands: the Independent State of Samoa, on Upolu, Savai'i and nearby islands

facts.text: Women and master weavers have formed fine mat committees in their villages, and more young women, and some men, now weave the 'ie Samoa.

source.title: 'Ie Samoa, fine mat and its cultural value

facts.text: Samoa's 2021 census counted 16,082 people aged 21 and over who hold a matai, or chiefly, title, including 1,444 women.

source.title: Samoa Population and Housing Census 2021 Fact Sheet (Final Results, October 2022)

nations.name: Chuukese
nations.lands: Chuuk State in the Federated States of Micronesia, on the high islands of Chuuk Lagoon such as Weno, Tonoas, Uman and Fefan, and outlying atolls

facts.text: Chuuk's state constitution says existing Chuukese custom and tradition shall be respected, and lets traditional leaders hold formal roles in government.

source.title: Chuuk State Constitution, Article IV
source.publisher: Legal Information System of the Federated States of Micronesia

facts.text: Chuuk's constitution recognizes traditional rights over all reefs, tidelands and other submerged lands, including the water above them.

source.title: Chuuk State Constitution, Article IV
source.publisher: Legal Information System of the Federated States of Micronesia

nations.name: Palauans
nations.lands: the Republic of Palau in the western Pacific, with 16 states on Babeldaob, Koror and other islands

facts.text: Palauans still use the Rock Islands Southern Lagoon, a World Heritage site since 2012, for cultural purposes under a traditional governance system.
Palau's Council of Chiefs, made up of the highest traditional chiefs from each state, advises the President on traditional laws and customs.

nations.name: Gunantuna
nations.lands: the Gazelle Peninsula of New Britain Island, East New Britain Province, Papua New Guinea

facts.text: Diwarra pays for everyday things such as store goods and school fees, and sharing it out expresses ties between clans and individuals.

source.title: Gunantuna (Tolai people)
source.publisher: Queensland Art Gallery | Gallery of Modern Art

facts.text: In 2016 a Queensland gallery commissioned A Bit na Ta, a collaborative work made with the wider Tolai community whose music carries the rhythms of Tolai life from 1875 to 1975.

source.title: Art from Papua New Guinea Celebrated in Major QAG Exhibition
source.publisher: Queensland Art Gallery | Gallery of Modern Art

nations.name: Whanganui Iwi
nations.lands: The Whanganui River, from the mountains to the sea, North Island, Aotearoa New Zealand

facts.text: Ngā Tāngata Tiaki o Whanganui, the iwi river trust, was established in August 2014 with the signing of Ruruku Whakatupua.

source.title: Home | Ngā Tāngata Tiaki o Whanganui

facts.text: Since 2017, New Zealand law has recognised the Whanganui River, Te Awa Tupua, as a legal person, with a guardian office that acts as its human face.

source.title: The Whanganui River (Te Awa Tupua)
source.publisher: OsloMet (Oslo Metropolitan University), River Rights project

nations.name: Ngāi Tahu
nations.lands: Te Waipounamu (the South Island), Aotearoa New Zealand

facts.text: There are 18 Papatipu Rūnanga, local Ngāi Tahu councils, spread throughout Te Waipounamu, the South Island.

source.title: Ngāi Tahu | Te Rūnanga o Ngāi Tahu

facts.text: Ngāi Tahu means people of Tahu, and whakapapa, the ancestral link, binds all Ngāi Tahu whānau.

source.title: Ngāi Tahu | Te Rūnanga o Ngāi Tahu

nations.name: Nauruans
nations.lands: the island of Nauru, officially styled Naoero, in the central Pacific

facts.text: Nauru's government now presents the country as the Republic of Naoero on its official website.

source.title: The Government of the Republic of Naoero
source.publisher: Government of the Republic of Nauru

facts.text: In Nauru's 2021 census, 69 percent of residents aged 5 and over spoke only Nauruan at home, and another 25.3 percent spoke it with another language.

source.title: Nauru 2021 Population and Housing Census: Analytical Report

nations.name: Ngāti Whātua Ōrākei
nations.lands: Central Tāmaki Makaurau (Auckland), Aotearoa New Zealand

facts.text: Ngāti Whātua Ōrākei's shared affairs are looked after by their Trust and two subsidiaries: Whai Māia, the social arm, and Whai Rawa, the commercial arm.
Ngāti Whātua Ōrākei are the tangata whenua, the people of the land, of Te Kahu Tōpuni o Tuperiri in central Tāmaki Makaurau (Auckland).

nations.name: Refaluwasch
nations.lands: Saipan and other islands of the Commonwealth of the Northern Mariana Islands, a United States commonwealth in the western Pacific

facts.text: In December 2020 the Matawal Wóól Display Hall opened with photos and crafts made by students of the Tepengi Kkosch Refaluwasch culture program.

source.title: Carolinian Affairs Office 2021 Citizen Centric Report

facts.text: The Carolinian Affairs Office, created by the CNMI Constitution, advises the governor and works to protect and preserve the culture and traditions of Indigenous Carolinians.

source.title: Carolinian Affairs Office 2020 Citizen Centric Report

nations.name: Pohnpeians
nations.lands: Pohnpei State in the Federated States of Micronesia, on Pohnpei island and its outlying atolls

facts.text: Nan Madol, a World Heritage site since 2016, is traditionally owned and managed under the Nahnmwarki system, a chiefly institution that continues in Pohnpei today.

source.title: Nan Madol: Ceremonial Centre of Eastern Micronesia

facts.text: Pohnpei State's constitution protects the customs and traditions of Pohnpei's traditional kingdoms alongside its elected government.

source.title: Pohnpei
source.publisher: Legal Information System of the Federated States of Micronesia

nations.name: Delaware Nation
nations.lands: Anadarko, Oklahoma, United States; Lenape homelands on the Eastern Seaboard

facts.text: Delaware Nation is a federally recognized tribe based in Anadarko, Oklahoma.
In December 2022 Delaware Nation re-established its Tribal Historic Preservation Office to identify and protect cultural resources in Lenape homelands.

source.title: Delaware Nation Re-Established THPO Status with the National Park Services and US Department of Interior

nations.name: Wampanoag Tribe of Gay Head (Aquinnah)
nations.lands: Aquinnah, on the western end of Martha's Vineyard (Noepe), Massachusetts, United States

facts.text: The Aquinnah Wampanoag care for 477 acres of their ancestral lands on Martha's Vineyard.
In 1998 the town of Gay Head returned to its former Wampanoag name, Aquinnah.

nations.name: Tuscarora Nation
nations.lands: Tuscarora Nation territory near Lewiston, western New York, United States; earlier homelands in what is now North Carolina

facts.text: The Tuscarora Language Program works with one clear mission: to revive a community of Tuscarora speakers.
The Tuscarora Environment Program works as part of the Haudenosaunee Environmental Task Force, established in 1992 by the Grand Council.

nations.name: Mashpee Wampanoag Tribe
nations.lands: Mashpee on Cape Cod, Massachusetts, United States; Wampanoag homelands across present-day Massachusetts and eastern Rhode Island

facts.text: The Mashpee Wampanoag were re-acknowledged as a federally recognized tribe in 2007.

source.title: Mashpee Wampanoag Tribe | People of the First Light

facts.text: Children at Mukayuhsak Weekuw, the Mashpee Wampanoag language nest, could be the first in centuries to grow up proficient in Wôpanâak.

nations.name: Chickahominy Indian Tribe
nations.lands: the Chickahominy River area and Chickahominy Ridge in Virginia, as described in the Tribe's history

facts.text: The Chickahominy Indian Tribe's history describes permanent villages along the Virginia river that still bears its name.
The Tribe dates the establishment of Samaria Indian Baptist Church, a community institution, to 1901.

nations.name: United Keetoowah Band of Cherokee Indians in Oklahoma
nations.lands: Tahlequah, Oklahoma, United States

facts.text: The UKB Tribal Council is made up of four officers and nine district representatives, governing from Tahlequah, Oklahoma.

source.title: United Keetoowah Band | Home | Tahlequah, OK
source.publisher: United Keetoowah Band of Cherokee Indians in Oklahoma

facts.text: The United Keetoowah Band numbers more than 14,000 tribal members today.

source.title: About Us | United Keetoowah Band | Tahlequah
source.publisher: United Keetoowah Band of Cherokee Indians in Oklahoma

pronounce.publisher: United Keetoowah Band of Cherokee Indians in Oklahoma, on its own site

nations.name: Monacan Indian Nation
nations.lands: Bear Mountain in Amherst County, Virginia; the Nation describes ancestral homelands extending through Virginia and parts of West Virginia and North Carolina

facts.text: The Nation says its Priority Climate Action Plan includes a greenhouse gas inventory to guide conservation and emissions-reduction work.
The Nation describes its citizens as descendants of Virginia and North Carolina Eastern Siouan cultural and linguistic groups.

nations.name: Nansemond Indian Nation
nations.lands: the Nansemond River area of southeastern Virginia; the Nation describes traditional settlements extending into northeastern North Carolina

facts.text: The Nation's published Environmental Program describes oyster restoration, invasive plant removal and native plant restoration.
The Nation's history dates formal organization with elected officers to 1984.

nations.name: Muscogee Nation
nations.lands: Okmulgee and the Muscogee reservation in eastern Oklahoma, United States; original homelands in present-day Georgia and Alabama

facts.text: Seated in Okmulgee, Oklahoma, the Muscogee (Creek) Nation is self-governed and organized by its Constitution into three branches of government.
The Mvskoke Language Program offers classes and learning resources so Mvskoke people can keep their language, culture and sovereignty strong.

nations.name: Chickahominy Indian Tribe - Eastern Division
nations.lands: New Kent County, Virginia; the Tribe describes roots in Virginia before English colonization

facts.text: In its food-sovereignty account, CIT-ED says a 2022 EPA grant supported a community compost and gardening program.
The Tribe's timeline records a certificate of incorporation for the Chickahominy Indians Eastern Division in 1925.

nations.name: Narragansett Indian Tribe
nations.lands: Rhode Island, United States

facts.text: The Narragansett Indian Tribe received federal recognition and acknowledgement on April 11, 1983.
A land claim brought by the Tribe ended in a 1978 out-of-court settlement of about 1,800 acres.

nations.name: Sappony
nations.lands: the High Plains Indian Settlement along the North Carolina-Virginia boundary, including Person County, North Carolina, and Halifax County, Virginia, as described by Sappony

facts.text: Sappony describes committees addressing education, cultural preservation and economic development.
Sappony's governance page describes a council with one elected representative from each of the settlement's seven families.

nations.name: The Chickasaw Nation
nations.lands: Thirteen counties in south-central Oklahoma, United States; original homelands in present-day Mississippi, Alabama and Tennessee

facts.text: The Chickasaw Nation's three-department government was reestablished with the ratification of its 1983 Constitution.
The Chickasaw language revitalization program began in 2007, and its master-apprentice program pairs learners with fluent Chickasaw speakers.

nations.name: Catawba Nation
nations.lands: York County, South Carolina, near Rock Hill, with a service area that includes North Carolina, United States

facts.text: After a 20-year effort, a land claim settlement on November 20, 1993 brought the Catawba Indian Nation federal recognition.
The Catawba Nation has over 3,300 enrolled citizens and continues to grow.

nations.name: Haliwa-Saponi Indian Tribe

source.title: Cultural Classes - Haliwa Saponi Tribe Resources

nations.name: Waccamaw Siouan Tribe

nations.name: Onondaga Nation
nations.lands: Onondaga Nation territory south of Syracuse, central New York, United States

facts.text: In the Haudenosaunee Grand Council, the Onondaga Fire Keepers present an issue, and debate goes on until they can announce that all are of One Mind, a decision by consensus.

nations.name: Cayuga Nation
nations.lands: Around Cayuga Lake in the Finger Lakes region of New York, United States

facts.text: After more than 200 years away, Cayuga Nation citizens once again live on their ancestral homeland in New York's Finger Lakes region.

nations.name: Pamunkey Indian Tribe
nations.lands: Pamunkey Reservation on the Pamunkey River, King William County, Virginia, United States

facts.text: The U.S. Department of the Interior acknowledged the Pamunkey Indian Tribe as federally recognized, effective January 28, 2016.
The Pamunkey reservation sits on the northern bank of the Pamunkey River in King William County, Virginia.

nations.name: Cherokee Tribe of Northeast Alabama
nations.lands: Northeast Alabama; its own introduction traces its roots to the lower Cherokee towns.

facts.text: Its government page describes a Tribal Council with one representative for each district.
Its Learning Tools page presents a syllabary song and a public word-learning list.

nations.name: Upper Mattaponi Tribe
nations.lands: King William County, Virginia; the Tribe describes its community base as within the traditional lands of Tsenacomacah

facts.text: The Tribe's school history says King William County returned Sharon Indian School to the Tribe in 1987.

source.title: Sharon Indian School Foundation - Upper Mattaponi Tribe

facts.text: The Tribe's history says the Adamstown band became officially known as the Upper Mattaponi Tribe in 1921.

nations.name: Northern Cheyenne Tribe

nations.name: Comanche Nation
nations.lands: Southwest Oklahoma, United States; headquarters north of Lawton

facts.text: The Comanche Nation's main governing body is its Tribal Council, made up of every enrolled member over age 18.
The Comanche Nation language program works to revitalize and reclaim the Comanche language, including through online learning.

nations.name: Apsáalooke Nation
nations.lands: Crow Indian Reservation, south-central Montana, United States; headquarters at Crow Agency

facts.text: The Apsáalooke Nation's government has three branches: executive, legislative and judicial.

source.title: Crow Nation
source.publisher: Montana Governor's Office of Indian Affairs

nations.name: Spirit Lake Nation
nations.lands: Northeastern North Dakota, mainly Benson County, United States; headquarters at Fort Totten

facts.text: Cankdeska Cikana Community College, the tribal college at Spirit Lake, offers 12 associate degree and certificate programs.

source.title: Spirit Lake Nation | Indian Affairs Commission, North Dakota

facts.text: At Spirit Lake both English and the Dakota language are spoken, specifically the Eastern Dakota dialect.

source.title: Spirit Lake Nation | Indian Affairs Commission, North Dakota

nations.name: Ponca Tribe of Nebraska
nations.lands: Fifteen-county service area across Nebraska, Iowa and South Dakota, United States

facts.text: The tribe serves its people across a fifteen-county service area in Nebraska, Iowa and South Dakota, set up by the Ponca Restoration Act.
The Ponca Restoration Act, signed by President George H. W. Bush, restored federal recognition to the Ponca Tribe of Nebraska.

nations.name: Cheyenne River Sioux Tribe
nations.lands: Cheyenne River Reservation, central South Dakota, United States; headquarters in Eagle Butte

nations.name: Iowa Tribe of Kansas and Nebraska

source.publisher: Iowa Tribe of Kansas and Nebraska

nations.name: Mandan, Hidatsa, and Arikara Nation

source.title: MHA Nation | Mandan, Hidatsa, and Arikara Nation

nations.name: Northern Arapaho Tribe

nations.name: Sac and Fox Nation
nations.lands: Central Oklahoma, United States; headquarters in Stroud

facts.text: The Sac and Fox Nation supports learning Sauk through an interactive language website and a concise Sauk dictionary.

nations.name: Bay Mills Indian Community
nations.lands: the Bay Mills Reservation in Michigan

source.title: History Department: Bay Mills Indian Community

nations.name: Cheyenne and Arapaho Tribes

facts.text: The Cheyenne and Arapaho Language Program offers classes in tribal communities and online for tribal members.

source.title: Language and Culture | Cheyenne and Arapaho Tribes

nations.name: Meskwaki Nation
also: Sac & Fox Tribe of the Mississippi in Iowa
nations.lands: Meskwaki Settlement near Tama, Iowa, United States

facts.text: The Meskwaki Nation has its own constitution, codified laws, police officers and a fully functioning court system.

source.title: History | Meskwaki | Sac & Fox Tribe of the Mississippi
source.publisher: Sac & Fox Tribe of the Mississippi in Iowa

source.title: History | Meskwaki | Sac & Fox Tribe of the Mississippi

nations.name: Shakopee Mdewakanton Sioux Community

nations.name: Caddo Nation of Oklahoma

nations.name: Oglala Sioux Tribe
nations.lands: Pine Ridge Reservation, southwestern South Dakota, United States

nations.name: Omaha Tribe of Nebraska

nations.name: Mille Lacs Band of Ojibwe

nations.name: Secwépemc
nations.lands: Secwepemcúl’ecw, a large territory in the interior of British Columbia, Canada, stretching from the Columbia River valley west to the Fraser River

facts.text: The Shuswap Nation Tribal Council brings together nine Secwépemc communities in the Southern Interior of British Columbia.
Secwépemc Chiefs formed the Shuswap Nation Tribal Council in 1980 to advance Aboriginal rights, self-government and the settlement of land title.

nations.name: Anishinabek Nation
nations.lands: 39 First Nations across Ontario, Canada, from Pikwàkanagàn in the east and Aamjiwnaang in the south to Lake Nipigon in the north

facts.text: It is Ontario's oldest political organization, with roots in the Confederacy of Three Fires that long predates European contact.
The Anishinabek Nation speaks for 39 First Nations in Ontario with about 70,000 citizens, roughly one third of the province's First Nation population.

nations.name: Dene
nations.lands: Denendeh, the western Northwest Territories, Canada

facts.text: The Dene Nation brings together five regional groups, the Gwich'in, Sahtú, Deh Cho, Tłı̨chǫ and Akaitcho Dene, each with its own language and territory.
Dene simply means 'the people'. Their homeland, Denendeh, lies in the western Northwest Territories.

nations.name: Labrador Inuit
nations.lands: Nunatsiavut, on the north coast of Labrador, Canada

facts.text: Nunatsiavut's legislative capital is Hopedale and its administrative capital is Nain.
The Nunatsiavut Government, the self-government of Labrador Inuit, officially came into being on December 1, 2005.

nations.name: Nisg̱a’a Nation
nations.lands: The Nass River Valley (K’alii-Aksim-Lisims) in northwestern British Columbia, Canada

facts.text: The Nisg̱a’a, People of the Nass River, are a self-governing First Nation on Canada's Pacific Coast.
The Nisg̱a’a Final Agreement was the first modern treaty in British Columbia, and it recognizes both Nisg̱a’a Lands and the Nisg̱a’a Government.

nations.name: Métis Nation
nations.lands: The Métis Nation Homeland as described by the Métis National Council: Manitoba, Saskatchewan and Alberta, plus parts of Ontario, British Columbia, the Northwest Territories and the northern United States

facts.text: Many historic Métis communities still stand along rivers and lakes once tied to fur trade posts, and many Métis citizens live in cities within the Homeland.
The Métis emerged as a distinct Indigenous people with their own culture, traditions, nationhood and language, Michif.

nations.name: Ktunaxa
nations.lands: ʔamakʔis Ktunaxa: the Kootenay region of southeastern British Columbia, Canada, with Kootenay Tribes also based today in Montana and Idaho, United States

facts.text: The Ktunaxa Nation Council helps represent the shared interests of four Ktunaxa First Nations within ʔamakʔis Ktunaxa, the Ktunaxa homelands.
ʔamakʔis Ktunaxa, the traditional territory, covers about 70,000 square kilometres in the Kootenay region of southeastern British Columbia.

nations.name: Mi’kmaq
nations.lands: Mi’kma’ki: Nova Scotia, New Brunswick, Prince Edward Island, Newfoundland and the Gaspé in Canada, with relatives in Maine, United States

facts.text: Mi'kmaw communities in Nova Scotia wrote their own Netukulimk Livelihood Management Plans so members who fish can support themselves and their families.
In 2006 the 13 Mi'kmaw Chiefs of Nova Scotia formed the Assembly of Nova Scotia Mi'kmaw Chiefs to guide the Nation's negotiators on rights and title.

nations.name: Tsuut’ina Nation
nations.lands: Treaty 7 territory in southern Alberta, Canada, bordering the city of Calgary

facts.text: Tsuut'ina Nation describes itself today as a highly sufficient and economically advanced First Nation.
Tsuut'ina is the only Dene-speaking nation in Treaty 7 territory, linked to the wider Dene Nation by its Athabaskan language.

nations.name: Vuntut Gwitchin First Nation
nations.lands: Old Crow and the surrounding homeland in northern Yukon, Canada

facts.text: Old Crow, a fly-in community of about 300 people on the Porcupine River, is the seat of the Vuntut Gwitchin government.
Dinjii Zhuh k'yuu, the Gwich'in language, is the official language of the Vuntut Gwitchin First Nation, which is training teachers and raising young speakers.

nations.name: Southern Ute Indian Tribe
nations.lands: Southern Ute Reservation around Ignacio, southwestern Colorado, United States

facts.text: The Southern Ute Indian Tribe is made up of the Mouache and Caputa bands and is headquartered in Ignacio, Colorado.
An elected Tribal Council governs the Southern Ute Indian Tribe, which maintains its own constitution, laws and tribal courts.

nations.name: San Carlos Apache
nations.lands: Gila, Graham and Pinal counties, southeastern Arizona, US

facts.text: The San Carlos Apache Reservation, set aside in 1871, covers 1,834,781 acres reaching from alpine meadows to desert in southeastern Arizona.
More than a third of San Carlos land is forest or woodland, giving a home to elk, mule deer, black bear, turkeys and mountain lion.

nations.name: A:shiwi
nations.lands: Pueblo of Zuni along the Zuni River in western New Mexico, US, with reservation land in Arizona

facts.text: The Pueblo of Zuni counts about 18,692 people and holds about 463,287 acres of reservation land.
For about the last 300 years most Zuni people have lived in one main village, the Pueblo of Zuni, with farming villages used at planting and harvest.

nations.name: Lipan Apache Tribe
nations.lands: Texas, United States, with tribal administration in McAllen and historical homelands spanning Texas and northern Mexico

facts.text: The Lipan Apache Tribe in Texas maintains a Tribal Council responsible for community welfare and protection of its heritage.
In 2021, the City and County of Presidio donated a Lipan cemetery parcel to the Lipan Apache Tribe.

source.title: El Cementerio de los Lipanes Transferred to Tribe

nations.name: Ute Indian Tribe
also: Ute Indian Tribe of the Uintah and Ouray Reservation
nations.lands: Uintah and Ouray Reservation, northeastern Utah, with tribal government at Fort Duchesne, United States

facts.text: In an April 2026 statement, the Ute Indian Tribe announced it would appeal a federal district court decision concerning split-estate reservation lands.

source.title: Tribe will appeal Utah Federal District Court decision on split estate lands

facts.text: The Ute Indian Tribe elects Business Committee representatives from the Uintah, Uncompahgre and Whiteriver bands.

nations.name: Taos Pueblo
nations.lands: Taos valley, northern New Mexico, US

facts.text: Tiwa is the native language of Taos Pueblo, and English and Spanish are also spoken there.
In 1970 a federal law returned 48,000 acres, including Blue Lake, to Taos Pueblo, a landmark for tribal self-determination across the United States.

nations.name: Wixárika
nations.lands: Sierra Madre Occidental in Jalisco and Nayarit, Mexico, with communities in Durango and Zacatecas

facts.text: At the end of the 1700s Wixárika communities received land titles that defined the boundaries of their present-day communities.

source.title: Huicholes
source.publisher: Sistema de Información Cultural, Secretaría de Cultura (Mexico)

facts.text: In July 2025 UNESCO added the Wixárika Route through sacred sites to Wirikuta, a 500 km corridor, to the World Heritage List after decades of Wixaritari requests.

source.title: Boletín No. 334: La Ruta Wixárika por los sitios sagrados a Wirikuta es inscrita en la Lista de Patrimonio Mundial de la UNESCO
source.publisher: Instituto Nacional de Antropología e Historia (INAH)

nations.name: Acoma
nations.lands: Acoma Mesa and surrounding lands in west-central New Mexico, US

facts.text: Since 2017 the Acoma Language Program has been building a Keres dictionary, with about 5,000 words and phrases being edited by fluent speakers.
In 1999 Acoma set up a Historic Preservation Office to keep traditional skills alive, among them stone cutting, wood carving, pottery making and weaving.

nations.name: Southern Paiute
nations.lands: Southern Utah and northern Arizona, US, including Cedar City, Utah, and the Kaibab reservation near Fredonia, Arizona

facts.text: The Paiute Indian Tribe of Utah Restoration Act of April 3, 1980 brought formal federal recognition to the Cedar Band of Paiute Indians.
The Paiute Indian Tribe of Utah shares The Paiute Language for Beginners, now in its second edition, which anyone can view and download.

nations.name: Rarámuri
nations.lands: Sierra Tarahumara in Chihuahua, Mexico, with smaller communities in Durango, Sonora and Sinaloa

facts.text: Rarámuri artisans make violins, drums, palm baskets, clay pots and wooden masks, and sell them in towns such as Guachochi, Creel and Batopilas.

source.title: Tarahumaras
source.publisher: Sistema de Información Cultural, Secretaría de Cultura (Mexico)

facts.text: The Rarámuri ball race is a contest in which runners cover long distances while kicking a wooden ball, and it is held as part of community fiestas.

source.title: Tarahumaras
source.publisher: Sistema de Información Cultural, Secretaría de Cultura (Mexico)

nations.name: Tohono O’odham
nations.lands: Sonoran Desert of southern Arizona, US (Sells is the capital), with O’odham communities across the border in Sonora, Mexico

facts.text: Divided by the border since the 1850s, O’odham communities in Sonora, Mexico, and Arizona still share a common culture and sense of being one people.

source.title: Pápagos
source.publisher: Sistema de Información Cultural, Secretaría de Cultura (Mexico)

facts.text: O’odham groups still speak the O’odham language, part of the Uto-Aztecan family, with dialects that vary from group to group.

nations.name: Hopi
nations.lands: Hopitutskwa, northeastern Arizona, US (Navajo and Coconino counties)

facts.text: Hopi government is unicameral. Its powers rest with a Tribal Council of village representatives, who serve two year terms.
The Hopi Reservation in northeastern Arizona covers more than 1.5 million acres and is made up of 12 villages on three mesas.

source.title: The Official Website of the Hopi Tribe

nations.name: Kha’P’o
nations.lands: From the eastern Jemez Mountains to the Rio Grande, northern New Mexico, US

facts.text: People of Santa Clara Pueblo still speak the Tewa language today and carry on their customs and cultural activities.
Santa Clara is one of six Tewa-speaking villages, and its reservation covers about 90 square miles from the Jemez Mountains to the Rio Grande.

nations.name: Kumeyaay
nations.lands: San Diego and Imperial counties, California, US, and Tecate, Ensenada and Rosarito in Baja California, Mexico

facts.text: North of the US and Mexico border there are 12 Kumeyaay Nation bands today, each original to Kumeyaay territory. Sycuan is one of them.

source.title: History & Heritage
source.publisher: Sycuan Band of the Kumeyaay Nation

facts.text: In Baja California the Kumiai call themselves Tipai. Their communities sit on the coastal plateaus of Ensenada and Rosarito and in Tecate.

source.title: Kumiais
source.publisher: Sistema de Información Cultural, Secretaría de Cultura (Mexico)

nations.name: Yoeme
nations.lands: Yaqui River valley in Sonora, Mexico, and Pascua Yaqui communities near Tucson, Arizona, US

facts.text: Most Yoeme people today live in the Mexican states of Sonora and Sinaloa, and the federally recognized Pascua Yaqui Tribe is based in Tucson, Arizona.
The Pascua Yaqui Tribe in Arizona gained United States federal recognition on September 18, 1978.

nations.name: Chiricahua Apache Nation
nations.lands: Headquarters in Santa Clara, New Mexico, United States; this record describes this named community, not every Chiricahua Apache person or government

facts.text: The Chiricahua Apache Nation lists its tribal headquarters in Santa Clara, New Mexico.
Its foundation's stated work includes education, social welfare and defending Chiricahua Apache self-determination.

nations.name: Augustine Band of Cahuilla Indians
also: Augustine Band of Cahuilla Indians, California
nations.lands: the Coachella Valley in southern California

facts.text: Its environmental page describes a Tribal Environmental Protection Agency established to develop and carry out environmental programs.

source.title: Tribal EPA - Augustine Band of Cahuilla Indians

facts.text: Its stewardship account dates the development of a renewable-energy operation to 2008.

source.title: Stewardship - Augustine Band of Cahuilla Indians

nations.name: Timbisha Shoshone Tribe
nations.lands: Death Valley and surrounding areas of California and Nevada

facts.text: Today the federally recognized Timbisha Shoshone Tribe works to keep its language, traditions and sovereignty strong.

source.title: Timbisha Shoshone Tribe - California and Nevada

facts.text: The Timbisha, part of the larger Western Shoshone people, have lived in Death Valley and its surrounding areas for thousands of years, and their village sits inside Death Valley National Park.

source.title: Timbisha Shoshone Tribe - California and Nevada

nations.name: Cahuilla Band of Indians
nations.lands: Anza area, Riverside County, Southern California

facts.text: The Band describes itself as a sovereign nation that carries its culture forward through strong governance.
Cahuilla traditional territory spans a large area of what are now Riverside and San Diego counties.

pronounce.text: kuh-WEE-eh (written on the Band's site as kəˊwi:e)
pronounce.publisher: Cahuilla Band of Indians, on its own site

nations.name: Washoe Tribe of Nevada and California
nations.lands: Lake Tahoe region and nearby valleys of western Nevada and eastern California

facts.text: Washoe teachers hold language classes for adults and youth four days a week, and immersion classes reach children in the tribe's Head Start.

source.title: Where Wašiw is Spoken: The Washoe Tribe is Passing Its Unique Language On and Up
source.publisher: Smithsonian National Museum of the American Indian (American Indian magazine)

facts.text: The name Tahoe is thought to come from Da ow ga, the Washoe word for lake.

source.title: Discover History
source.publisher: USDA Forest Service, Lake Tahoe Basin Management Unit

nations.name: Confederated Tribes and Bands of the Yakama Nation
nations.lands: South-central Washington State, around Mount Adams and tributaries of the Columbia River

facts.text: The Yakama Nation shares an Ichishkiin word each day to help learners build fluency in the language, also called Sahaptin.

source.title: Ichishkiin Word of the Day: Learn New Vocabulary | Yakama Nation
source.publisher: Confederated Tribes and Bands of the Yakama Nation

facts.text: The Yakama Reservation in Washington State spans about 1,130,000 acres.

source.title: About
source.publisher: Confederated Tribes and Bands of the Yakama Nation

nations.name: Santa Ynez Band of Chumash Indians
nations.lands: Santa Ynez Valley, Santa Barbara County, California

facts.text: The Tribe's Culture Department founded its language program in 2008, and the Tribe has unveiled a Samala-English Dictionary.

source.title: Culture
source.publisher: Santa Ynez Band of Chumash Indians

facts.text: Established on December 27, 1901, the Santa Ynez Reservation began with 99 acres and has grown to more than 1,500 acres.

source.title: The Santa Ynez Reservation
source.publisher: Santa Ynez Band of Chumash Indians

nations.name: Tongva
nations.lands: Greater Los Angeles region of California, a homeland called Tovaangar

facts.text: The conservancy, a Tongva-led nonprofit and not a tribal government, serves Tongva people, the wider Native community and guests, called kuuyam.
In 2022 Huhuunga, a one-acre parcel in Altadena, was returned to Tongva stewardship. It is now home to the Tongva-led Tongva Taraxat Paxaavxa Conservancy.

nations.name: Muckleshoot Indian Tribe
nations.lands: South King County, Washington, in the Puget Sound region; ancestors include Duwamish and Upper Puyallup peoples

facts.text: The Muckleshoot Indian Tribe is one of South King County's largest employers, supporting about 3,300 direct jobs.
Among Puget Sound tribes, Muckleshoot is the only one holding rights under two treaties.

nations.name: Tulalip Tribes
nations.lands: Tulalip Indian Reservation on Puget Sound, Snohomish County, Washington

facts.text: The Tulalip Lushootseed Language Department works toward every tribal home, workplace, gathering and classroom being rich in Lushootseed.
The Tulalip Tribes count over 5,100 people, about 2,700 of whom live on the 22,000-acre Tulalip Indian Reservation.

pronounce.publisher: Tulalip Tribes, on its own site

nations.name: Lummi Nation
nations.lands: Northernmost coast of Washington State and the waters of Puget Sound, with ancestral lands reaching into southern British Columbia

facts.text: Northwest Indian College, with its main campus on the Lummi Reservation, is the only accredited tribal college serving Washington, Oregon and Idaho.

source.title: About | Northwest Indian College | Accredited Tribal College

facts.text: The Lhaq'temish, the Lummi People, describe themselves as fishers, hunters, gatherers and harvesters of the Puget Sound shores and waters.

nations.name: Karuk Tribe
nations.lands: Klamath River country of northern California, with tribal offices in Happy Camp

facts.text: The Karuk Language Program teaches all ages through community classes, school partnerships and immersion, linking learners with fluent speakers.
The Karuk People's Center in Happy Camp opened in September 2002 and holds a museum, library, basketweaving classroom and the language program office.

nations.name: Hoopa Valley Tribe
nations.lands: Hoopa Valley along the Trinity River, Humboldt County, northern California

facts.text: The Hoopa Valley Tribe runs its own Fisheries Department, which counts the harvest and spawning returns of salmon, steelhead, sturgeon and lamprey.
Tribal fisheries crews made major progress restoring the lower reaches of Supply Creek and Mill Creek between 2015 and 2018.

nations.name: Quinault Indian Nation
nations.lands: Southwestern corner of Washington's Olympic Peninsula, between the Olympic Mountains and the Pacific Ocean

facts.text: The Nation has a Taholah Village Relocation Master Plan that includes planning for an upper village, and its Planning Department is updating the plan for 2026.

source.title: Taholah Village Relocation | Quinault Indian Nation, WA

facts.text: The Quinault Language Department works to revitalize the Quinault language, with in-person classes in Taholah, Queets and Hoquiam.

source.title: Language Department | Quinault Indian Nation, WA

nations.name: Tuolumne Band of Me-Wuk Indians
nations.lands: Sierra Nevada foothills, Tuolumne County, California

facts.text: In January 2005 the Tribe opened the Tuolumne Me-Wuk Indian Health Center.

source.title: History - The Tuolumne Band of Me-Wuk Indians

facts.text: Tuolumne Rancheria began in 1910 with 289.52 acres; today the Tribe holds more than 1,700 acres of fee and trust land.

source.title: History - The Tuolumne Band of Me-Wuk Indians

nations.name: Swinomish Indian Tribal Community
nations.lands: Swinomish Reservation near La Conner, Skagit County, Washington

facts.text: The Swinomish Tribe monitors air quality in partnership with the EPA, with two major oil refineries right next to its reservation.
Swinomish monitors record real-time data on particulates, ozone and nitrogen dioxide, plus weather such as wind, temperature, humidity and precipitation.

nations.name: Baniwa
nations.lands: Içana river and the Upper Rio Negro in Amazonas, Brazil, and neighboring Colombia and Venezuela

facts.text: The Baniwa speak languages of the Arawak family along the Içana river.
Baniwa communities live where Brazil meets Colombia and Venezuela, along the Içana river in the Upper Rio Negro region.

nations.name: Wapichana
nations.lands: Northeastern Roraima, Brazil, and the South Rupununi in southwestern Guyana

facts.text: In 2012 Wapichan leaders in Guyana presented a community map and land plan titled Thinking Together for those Coming Behind Us.

source.title: Wapichan people in Guyana present territorial map and community proposals to save ancestral forests

facts.text: The Wapichana language is classified in the Arawak language family.

nations.name: Guarani Mbya
nations.lands: Villages across southern and southeastern Brazil, eastern Paraguay, Misiones province in Argentina, and near Montevideo in Uruguay

facts.text: The Comissão Guarani Yvyrupa, founded in 2006, brings together Guarani collectives in six states of southern and southeastern Brazil.
In Guarani, yvyrupa names the structure that holds up the land, recalling free movement across territory before today's borders.

nations.name: Sápara
nations.lands: Rainforest of Pastaza province in the Ecuadorian Amazon, straddling the border with Peru

facts.text: The Sápara live in a part of the Amazon rainforest that straddles Ecuador and Peru.

source.title: Oral heritage and cultural manifestations of the Zápara people

facts.text: Sápara knowledge of the forest shows in their rich vocabulary for plants and animals and in their knowledge of the forest's medicinal plants.

source.title: Oral heritage and cultural manifestations of the Zápara people

nations.name: Kuikuro
nations.lands: Upper Xingu, in the Xingu Indigenous Territory, Mato Grosso, Brazil

facts.text: Kuikuro is a southern Carib language.
Kuikuro remains a living, intact language, used by everyone in all domains except talking with outsiders.

nations.name: Ka'apor
nations.lands: Northern Maranhão, Brazil, in the Alto Turiaçu Indigenous Land

facts.text: Ka'apor communities have had a shared, standard sign language for communicating with deaf members of the community.
Ka'apor is a language of the Tupi-Guarani family.

nations.name: A'uwe
nations.lands: Eastern Mato Grosso, Brazil, in Indigenous lands such as Pimentel Barbosa, Marãiwatsédé, São Marcos and Sangradouro

facts.text: The A'uwe (Xavante) language belongs to the Jê family of the Macro-Jê language stock.
The Xavante numbered about 22,256 people in 2020.

nations.name: Pataxó
nations.lands: Villages in the far south of Bahia and the north of Minas Gerais, Brazil

facts.text: The Pataxó are rebuilding their language, Patxohã, through a major community effort.
Pataxó villages are spread across the far south of Bahia and the north of Minas Gerais.

nations.name: Macuxi
nations.lands: Fields and mountains of northern Roraima, Brazil, between the headwaters of the Branco and Rupununi rivers, extending into Guyana and Venezuela

facts.text: The Conselho Indígena de Roraima, founded in 1990, unites ten peoples including the Macuxi and Wapichana, with 270 of the state's 465 communities as members.
The Macuxi language belongs to the Carib language family.

nations.name: Ashaninka
nations.lands: Upper Juruá region of Acre, Brazil, including the Amônia, Breu and Envira rivers, near the Peruvian border

facts.text: Ashaninka of the Amônia river created their own association, Apiwtxa, in 1991; it was officially registered in 1993.
Ashenĩka, the people's own name, can be translated as my relatives, my folk or my people.

nations.name: Terena
nations.lands: Mato Grosso do Sul, with communities in Mato Grosso and São Paulo, Brazil

facts.text: Farming remains the main productive activity in Terena reserves.
Terena people living in cities are concentrated mainly in Campo Grande, and most of them keep strong ties with their reserves.

nations.name: Tikuna
nations.lands: Along the upper Solimões (Amazon) river in Amazonas, Brazil, and in neighboring Peru and Colombia

facts.text: Tikuna communities are spread across three countries: Brazil, Peru and Colombia.
Tikuna is a tonal language, considered genetically isolated, with a complex sound system and grammar.

nations.name: Shuar
nations.lands: Zamora Chinchipe, Morona Santiago and southern Pastaza provinces in the Ecuadorian Amazon

facts.text: In 2022 the Shuar Aratsim Center approved its own Life Plan after participatory community workshops.

source.title: Territory of the Shuar People
source.publisher: ReVista, Harvard Review of Latin America (David Rockefeller Center for Latin American Studies)

facts.text: The Interprovincial Federation of Shuar Centers (FICSH), founded in 1964, was one of the pioneering Indigenous organizations of the Amazon.

source.title: Territory of the Shuar People
source.publisher: ReVista, Harvard Review of Latin America (David Rockefeller Center for Latin American Studies)

nations.name: Achuar
nations.lands: Northern Loreto in Peru near the Ecuador border, and the neighboring Amazon of Ecuador

facts.text: Peru's Ministry of Culture has registered five interpreters and translators of the Achuar language.

source.title: Achuar | BDPI
source.publisher: Ministerio de Cultura del Perú, Base de Datos de Pueblos Indígenas u Originarios

facts.text: Achuar is a cross-border language, spoken in both Peru and Ecuador.

source.title: Achuar | BDPI
source.publisher: Ministerio de Cultura del Perú, Base de Datos de Pueblos Indígenas u Originarios

nations.name: Avá Guarani
nations.lands: Mato Grosso do Sul and Paraná in Brazil, and eastern Paraguay

facts.text: Guarani peoples, the Avá Guarani among them, live across a territory that spans regions of Brazil, Bolivia, Paraguay and Argentina.
The Avá Guarani, called Ñandeva in Brazil, have a present-day territory that takes in parts of Mato Grosso do Sul and Paraná.

source.title: Guarani Kaiowá - Povos Indígenas no Brasil

nations.name: Mam
nations.lands: Western highlands of Guatemala (Huehuetenango, San Marcos, Quetzaltenango) and neighboring Chiapas, Mexico

facts.text: In October 2025, the Mam communities of Cajolá and Todos Santos Cuchumatán joined two other Maya communities in reporting to a UN committee on their community radio rights.

source.title: Indigenous Communities and Cultural Survival Urge CERD to Address Community Radio Rights Violations in Guatemala

facts.text: B'alam Stereo in Cabricán, among the longer-running Indigenous stations in Guatemala's highlands, has served the Maya Mam since 1976, with work promoting education, health, water and justice.

source.title: Announcing Our 2019 Community Media Grants Partners

nations.name: Lokono
nations.lands: Coastal and river villages of Suriname, Guyana and French Guiana

facts.text: Suriname's association of Indigenous village leaders lists the Lokono among the country's four major Indigenous peoples, with villages such as Washabo, Apoera and Alfonsdorp.

source.title: Dorpen en Dorpsbesturen
source.publisher: Vereniging van Inheemse Dorpshoofden in Suriname (VIDS)

facts.text: Lokono village representatives founded Wadian Bokotothi, meaning 'Language Keepers', and helped share one common Lokono spelling across Suriname, French Guiana and Guyana.

source.title: State-of-the-Art in the Development of the Lokono Language
source.publisher: Language Documentation & Conservation, University of Hawai'i Press

nations.name: Ch'orti'
nations.lands: Jocotán, Camotán, Olopa and Quezaltepeque in Chiquimula and La Unión in Zacapa, Guatemala, and communities around Copán in Honduras

facts.text: Ch'orti' is also spoken in Honduran communities such as Cabañas, Santa Rita and Copán Ruinas.

source.title: Descubre los útiles escolares en idioma ch'orti'

facts.text: In 2025 the Academy of Mayan Languages of Guatemala translated the national symbols into Ch'orti'; the flag, for example, is tz'apray b'ujk.

source.title: Símbolos patrios en ch'orti: un aporte para preservar el idioma y la identidad

nations.name: Bribri
nations.lands: The Talamanca mountains of southern Costa Rica, on both the Caribbean (Limón) and Pacific (Puntarenas) sides, with smaller communities in Bocas del Toro, Panama

facts.text: The Bribri language is spoken on both sides of Costa Rica's Talamanca mountains, in Limón and Puntarenas, in three regional varieties named for Amubre, Coroma and Salitre.
Bribri communities also live in Panama, where the 2023 census counted 766 Bribri people.

source.title: Cuadro 20. Población indígena en la República, por sexo, según provincia, comarca indígena, grupo indígena al que pertenece y grupos de edad: Censo 2023
source.publisher: Instituto Nacional de Estadística y Censo (INEC), Panama

nations.name: Tz'utujil
nations.lands: The southern shore of Lake Atitlán in Sololá, Guatemala, including Santiago Atitlán and San Pedro La Laguna

facts.text: In Santiago Atitlán, a Tz'utujil traditional authority welcomed Indigenous youth from three countries in 2013 and spoke in Tz'utujil about the role of ancestral authorities.

source.title: Indigenous Mayan Youth Forge International Relationships Based on Community Radio

facts.text: Radio Sembrador, a community station in San Pedro La Laguna on Lake Atitlán, broadcasts news and cultural programs in Tz'utujil and Spanish.

source.title: Profile of A Community Radio Station: Radio Sembrador

nations.name: Ixil
nations.lands: The Ixil region of northern Quiché, Guatemala: Nebaj, Chajul and Cotzal

facts.text: Ixil women weavers of the Q'imb'al initiative, with youth and village ancestral authorities, launched Community Radio Tiichajil Tenam in Nebaj to share Ixil cultural values.

source.title: Radio Tiichajil Tenam Becomes a Reality

facts.text: In 2020 Guatemala's Constitutional Court ruled in favor of the Maya Ixil people of Nebaj, restoring their ownership of the communal land of Ak'ul.

source.title: Pueblos Mayas Ixiles y Ch'orti's recuperan certeza jurídica sobre sus tierras

nations.name: Kaqchikel
nations.lands: Central highlands of Guatemala, including Chimaltenango, Sacatepéquez and parts of Sololá

facts.text: Community Radio Naköj in Santo Domingo Xenacoj, working since 2013, produces programs in Kaqchikel and Spanish for about 7,000 Kaqchikel listeners.

source.title: 2020 Community Media COVID-19 Emergency Grant Partners

facts.text: In 2022 the United Nations Special Rapporteur on the Rights of Indigenous Peoples was a member of the Maya Kaqchikel people.

source.title: Historic Win: Inter-American Court of Human Rights Rules in Favor of Indigenous Peoples

nations.name: Kaliña
nations.lands: Coastal Suriname and French Guiana, with related communities in Guyana, Venezuela and Brazil

facts.text: In Suriname the Kari'na (Kaliña) live in many villages with their own village heads, including Christiaankondre and Langamankondre at Galibi in Marowijne district.

source.title: Dorpen en Dorpsbesturen
source.publisher: Vereniging van Inheemse Dorpshoofden in Suriname (VIDS)

facts.text: Suriname's Indigenous village leaders say legal recognition of collective rights is an obligation, not a policy choice, and in 2026 urged full implementation of the Kaliña and Lokono judgment.

source.title: VIDS dient resolutie in: Voer Kaliña & Lokono-vonnis uit
source.publisher: Vereniging van Inheemse Dorpshoofden in Suriname (VIDS)

nations.name: Nahuat Pipil
nations.lands: Western El Salvador, especially Sonsonate and Ahuachapán departments

facts.text: Izalco is the only municipality in El Salvador with an ancestral Indigenous government, made up of mayordomos and mayordomas.

source.title: Radio Sensunat: Broadcasting to Revitalize the Nahuat Language in El Salvador

facts.text: In Santo Domingo de Guzmán, Nahuat-speaking teachers created Nahuatl cribs where children learn the language, and Radio Sensunat promotes Nahuat Pipil culture.

source.title: Radio Sensunat: Broadcasting to Revitalize the Nahuat Language in El Salvador

nations.name: Wayuu
nations.lands: The Guajira Peninsula, shared by northern Colombia (La Guajira) and northwestern Venezuela (Zulia)

facts.text: Wayuu justice rests on dialogue: respected mediators called Pütchipü'üi, or palabreros, settle disputes between clans through repair and compensation. UNESCO listed this system in 2010.

source.title: Wayuu normative system, applied by the Pütchipü'üi (palabrero)

facts.text: The Wayuu live on the Guajira Peninsula, which spans the border between Colombia and Venezuela.

source.title: Wayuu normative system, applied by the Pütchipü'üi (palabrero)

nations.name: Ngäbe
nations.lands: The Ngäbe-Buglé comarca in western Panama (parts of Bocas del Toro, Chiriquí and Veraguas), nearby lands in Panama, and Ngäbe territories in southern Costa Rica

facts.text: Panama's Law 10 of 1997 created the Ngäbe-Buglé comarca and made its lands the collective property of the comarca, closed to private sale.

source.title: Ley 10 de 7 de marzo de 1997, por la cual se crea la Comarca Ngöbe-Buglé

facts.text: Panama's 2023 census counted 444,878 Ngäbe people.

source.title: Cuadro 20. Población indígena en la República, por sexo, según provincia, comarca indígena, grupo indígena al que pertenece y grupos de edad: Censo 2023

nations.name: Guna
nations.lands: Gunayala on Panama's Caribbean coast and islands, plus Madungandí and Wargandí in Panama and communities in northwestern Colombia

facts.text: Gunayala's 49 communities govern themselves together through the Guna General Congress, their highest political and administrative body for land, resources and education.

source.title: Gunayala: A Living Model of Autonomy and Self-government

facts.text: Gunayala runs along Panama's Caribbean coast to the Colombian border, with about 315 km of coastline and over 400 small islands and islets.

source.title: Gunayala: A Living Model of Autonomy and Self-government

nations.name: Emberá
nations.lands: The Emberá-Wounaan comarca and collective lands in Darién and eastern Panama, and the Pacific and Chocó regions of Colombia

facts.text: Panama's Law 22 of 1983 created the Emberá comarca in Darién and named its General Congress the highest traditional decision-making body of the Emberá people.

source.title: Ley 22 de 1983, por la cual se crea la Comarca Emberá de Darién
source.publisher: FAOLEX, Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations

facts.text: Bilingual storybooks in Emberá and Spanish are among the learning materials made for the early education of Emberá children in Panama.

source.title: La educación intercultural bilingüe en Panamá
source.publisher: UNICEF Latin America and the Caribbean

nations.name: Binnizá
nations.lands: The Isthmus of Tehuantepec, Oaxaca, Mexico, including Juchitán and Tehuantepec

facts.text: Velas, festivals honoring patron saints, family names, trades and places, are a central Binnizá institution; Juchitán alone celebrates about 24 of them.

source.title: Zapotecos (del Istmo, Valles centrales y Sierra Norte) : Pueblos indígenas México : Sistema de Información Cultural-Secretaría de Cultura
source.publisher: Secretaría de Cultura, Sistema de Información Cultural (SIC), Gobierno de México

nations.name: Tutunakú
nations.lands: The Totonacapan: northern Veracruz around Papantla and the Sierra Norte de Puebla, Mexico

facts.text: Community groups asked for radio in their own languages, and since 1994 La Voz de la Sierra Norte in Cuetzalan, Puebla has served Nahua and Totonac peoples.

source.title: XECTZ La Voz de la Sierra Norte (AM) : Radio cultural indígena México : Sistema de Información Cultural-Secretaría de Cultura
source.publisher: Secretaría de Cultura, Sistema de Información Cultural (SIC), with station information from INPI

facts.text: At the Centre for Indigenous Arts, Totonac is the language of teaching, and each art is taught in its own house-school, laid out like a traditional settlement.

source.title: Xtaxkgakget Makgkaxtlawana: the Centre for Indigenous Arts and its contribution to safeguarding the intangible cultural heritage of the Totonac people of Veracruz, Mexico

nations.name: Ayuuk
nations.lands: The Sierra Mixe of northeastern Oaxaca, Mexico, including Tlahuitoltepec, Tamazulapam, Ayutla and Guichicovi

facts.text: Backstrap loom weaving continues in Tamazulapam, Tlahuitoltepec and Cotzocón, and young Ayuuk artists are taking up mural and canvas painting.

source.title: Mixes : Pueblos indígenas México : Sistema de Información Cultural-Secretaría de Cultura
source.publisher: Secretaría de Cultura, Sistema de Información Cultural (SIC), Gobierno de México

source.title: Mixes : Pueblos indígenas México : Sistema de Información Cultural-Secretaría de Cultura
source.publisher: Secretaría de Cultura, Sistema de Información Cultural (SIC), Gobierno de México

nations.lands: Yucatán, Campeche and Quintana Roo, on Mexico's Yucatán Peninsula

source.title: XEPET La Voz de los Mayas (AM) : Radio cultural indígena México : Sistema de Información Cultural-Secretaría de Cultura
source.publisher: Secretaría de Cultura, Sistema de Información Cultural (SIC), with station information from INPI

nations.lands: La Chinantla in northeastern Oaxaca, Mexico, and resettled communities in Veracruz

source.title: XEOJN La Voz de la Chinantla (AM) : Radio cultural indígena México : Sistema de Información Cultural-Secretaría de Cultura
source.publisher: Secretaría de Cultura, Sistema de Información Cultural (SIC), with station information from INPI

source.title: Chinantecos : Pueblos indígenas México : Sistema de Información Cultural-Secretaría de Cultura

nations.name: Jñatrjo
nations.lands: The northwestern State of Mexico and eastern Michoacán, Mexico

facts.text: La Voz de la Sierra Oriente, on air since 1998 for Mazahua and Otomí communities, hosts poetry recitals and rock concerts in their own languages.

nations.lands: La Mixteca, in northwestern Oaxaca, southern Puebla and eastern Guerrero, Mexico, with migrant communities across Mexico and in the United States

source.title: XETLA La Voz de la Mixteca (AM) : Radio cultural indígena México : Sistema de Información Cultural-Secretaría de Cultura
source.publisher: Secretaría de Cultura, Sistema de Información Cultural (SIC), with station information from INPI

nations.lands: Southwestern Oaxaca, Mexico, near the Pacific coast, including Juquila, Yaitepec, Quiahije and Nopala

facts.text: Since 1994, La Voz de la Costa Chica in Santiago Jamiltepec, Oaxaca has broadcast in Mixtec, Amuzgo, Chatino, Tacuate and Spanish.

source.title: XEJAM La Voz de la Costa Chica (AM) : Radio cultural indígena México : Sistema de Información Cultural-Secretaría de Cultura
source.publisher: Secretaría de Cultura, Sistema de Información Cultural (SIC), with station information from INPI

source.title: Chatinos : Pueblos indígenas México : Sistema de Información Cultural-Secretaría de Cultura
source.publisher: Secretaría de Cultura, Sistema de Información Cultural (SIC), Gobierno de México

nations.name: O' de püt
nations.lands: Northwestern and central Chiapas, Mexico, including Copainalá, Ocotepec, Tapalapa, Tecpatán, Ocozocoautla and Tuxtla Gutiérrez

facts.text: Since 1997, the INPI station La Voz de los Vientos has broadcast from Copainalá, a town whose Zoque name is Pokiomä, in Zoque, Tsotsil and Spanish.

source.title: XECOPA La Voz de los Vientos (AM) : Radio cultural indígena México : Sistema de Información Cultural-Secretaría de Cultura
